To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the R substituent of isoniazids should contain a large flat plane, and both sides of this plane should contain an electro-positive group.

the R substituent of INH derivatives should contain a plane with an electroposive group on both sides of the planes and the 4-pyril ring of the INH derivatives should be sterically and electrostatically optimal.
the binding of INH-NAd and its derivative adducats in InhA pocket are dominated by hydrogen bond interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the drug-enzyme interactions and their structural basis for improving the affinity and potency of isoniazide and its derivatives.
the rational design of new and potentially more effective antituberculosis agents.
the elucidation of the structural basis of drug-enzyme interactions and the rational design of isoniazids and their derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3,4-dihydropyridine ring and the 4-piperidone ring are the most important pharmacophores for the antituberculous activity of isoniazids.
the R substituent of isoniazids should contain a large planar and the 4-pyril ring should have both steric and electro static fields.
INH derivatives with a larger plane and both sides containing an electropositivity group are more potent than INH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined use of quantum chemical calculation, molecular docking calculation, CoMFA, and CoMSIA is an effective approach in the rational design of novel isoniazid-based antituberculous agents.

the combination of molecular modeling approaches, quantum chemical calculations and experimental data can be a powerful and effective tool for elucidating drug–enzyme interactions and their structural basis.

the combined use of molecular docking, quantum chemical calculations, and CoMFA/CoMSIA methods is very useful for elucidating drug-enzyme interactions and their structural basis for designing more potent antituberculous drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combined use of structure-based and ligand-based design and quantum chemical calculations can be a powerful tool for elucidating drug-enzyme interactions and their structural basis for improving the affinity and potency of isoniazids and its derivatives.
the combined use of molecular docking calculations, quantum chemical calculations, and CoMFA/CoMSIA models can provide valuable insights for designing new and more effective antituberculosis agents.

the binding mode of INH-NDA adduct in InhA pocket can be predicted by molecular docking and the binding affinity of INH-NADA adducts in binding pocket can be predicted based on the CoMFA and/or CoMSIA models.
